record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: If a spacetime satisfies condition (G) when some point has a domain of influence meeting every inextendible timelike curve, does failure of condition (G), or the presence of a hidden infinity, in a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition force a trapped surface and thereby support the dichotomy that the spacetime is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R x M?

evidence.quote: A spacetime satisfies condition (G) if there is a point whose domain of influence meets every inextendible timelike curve [Gel;Gal;BR5]. Show that if condition (G) fails or there is a "hidden infinity" [BR5] in a cosmological spacetime V satisfying TCC, then there is a trapped surface in V. This would give a proof of Conjecture: Let V be a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition, Then either V is timelike geodesically incomplete or V splits as IRxM isometrically (and thus Vis static).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(V,g)$ be a cosmological spacetime, i.e., a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold with a compact Cauchy hypersurface satisfying the timelike convergence condition $\mathrm{Ric}(v,v)\ge 0$ for every timelike vector $v$. Say that $V$ satisfies condition (G) if there exists a point $p\in V$ whose domain of influence (the union of the chronological past and future of $p$) meets every inextendible timelike curve in $V$. Say further that $V$ has a "hidden infinity" if there exists an inextendible timelike curve which fails to enter the domain of influence of some point, in a way that no point of $V$ has its domain of influence intersecting every inextendible timelike curve.

Prove the following implication: if $V$ is a cosmological spacetime satisfying the timelike convergence condition and either condition (G) fails or $V$ contains a hidden infinity, then $V$ must contain a trapped surface.

As a consequence, derive the splitting dichotomy: every cosmological spacetime $V$ satisfying the timelike convergence condition is either timelike geodesically incomplete, or it splits isometrically as $(\mathbb{R}\times M, -dt^2\oplus h)$ for some compact Riemannian manifold $(M,h)$ (in which case $V$ is static).
artifact.status_search_result: Bartnik's splitting conjecture for cosmological spacetimes satisfying the timelike convergence condition remains open in general. Partial results exist under additional hypotheses (e.g., existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces, S-ray condition, no observer horizon, level set conditions, conformal symmetries), but the full conjecture, and in particular the proposed route via showing that failure of condition (G) or a hidden infinity forces a trapped surface, has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Bartnik's splitting conjecture: cosmological spacetime with TCC is either timelike geodesically incomplete or splits isometrically as R x M; partial results under additional assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is still being investigated; full conjecture not proven, only partial cases.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on conformal symmetries and Bartnik's splitting conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Bartnik's splitting conjecture, proved with additional assumptions such as S-ray or level set condition.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture remains open without additional assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Examples of cosmological spacetimes without CMC Cauchy surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2023) work continues to study cosmological spacetimes and obstructions related to Bartnik's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Active research area; conjecture not resolved.
